title: Evaluation
tagline: Benchmarks, contamination, human and model judges, capability evaluations and the statistics of evaluation
summary: Knowing what a model can do is surprisingly hard. This course covers benchmark evaluation and its pitfalls of contamination and saturation, human preference evaluation and arenas, models as judges, capability and dangerous-capability evaluations, robustness and calibration, and the statistics needed to compare models honestly.

chapters.title: Principles of evaluation
chapters.summary: What to measure, validity, and the gap between benchmarks and real use.

chapters.title: Benchmarks
chapters.summary: Knowledge, reasoning, coding and multilingual benchmarks and how they are scored.

chapters.title: Contamination and saturation
chapters.summary: Test-set leakage, how to detect it, and the life cycle of benchmarks.

chapters.title: Human evaluation and arenas
chapters.summary: Pairwise comparisons, Elo and Bradley–Terry ratings, and their biases.

chapters.title: Models as judges
chapters.summary: LLM-as-a-judge, rubrics, position and length bias, and agreement with humans.

chapters.title: Capability and dangerous-capability evaluations
chapters.summary: Eliciting capabilities, agentic tasks and evaluations for high-risk capabilities.

chapters.title: Statistics of evaluation
chapters.summary: Confidence intervals and significance, variance across seeds and prompts, and calibration.
